topic: Sukuna's barrierless Malevolent Shrine is why the domain clash with Gojo tilted his way
title: Why Gojo's Domain Broke Before Sukuna's Did
description: Gojo's Unlimited Void is the strongest domain in Jujutsu Kaisen, so why did it shatter first? The answer is a design choice in Sukuna's Malevolent Shrine that most fans skip past. Do you think Gojo was ever going to win that clash?
comment: Gojo vs Sukuna: was the domain clash decided by Sukuna's barrierless trick, or by Gojo's exhaustion? Pick one.

lines.text: Gojo's Unlimited Void should have won. So why did it break first?

shot.fallback: white haired sorcerer in a starry void

lines.text: People blame power, but I think it's design.

shot.fallback: two sorcerers facing off in ruined city

lines.text: A normal domain is a closed barrier, a little prison made of cursed energy.

shot.fallback: glowing sphere barrier in a city

lines.text: And that barrier is a weakness. You can crack it from outside.
Sukuna's Malevolent Shrine has no barrier at all.
He opens it right in the open air, so there is nothing to crack.

shot.fallback: demon king standing before a shrine

lines.text: Here's the detail most people forget.
During the clash, Sukuna shrank the Shrine's range to squeeze more power into every Cleave and Dismantle.
Gojo had to keep his whole barrier standing. Sukuna only had to keep cutting.

shot.fallback: two domains clashing over a city

lines.text: Yes, the Shrine collapsed at the end too. People say that proves they were equal.
But Gojo's barrier shattered first, and that's what decided the next move.
So the strongest domain lost to a domain with no walls.
Gojo's Unlimited Void should have won...

shot.fallback: white haired sorcerer in a starry void
